title: Clear the generated UE5 code when a new simulation replaces the result
body:
## Summary
After a second simulation run, EconomyCodeGenPanel keeps showing the files (and footer config) generated from the previous result.

## Description
src/stores/economySimulatorStore.ts:153 runSimulation sets result/metrics/alerts/supplyDemand/drift but never resets codeGenResult, so src/components/modules/evaluator/EconomyCodeGenPanel.tsx:306-310 renders code and a "Philosophy / Max Level / agents" footer for a run that is no longer on screen. Fixed = runSimulation clears codeGenResult (or the panel marks it stale when codeGenResult.config differs from result.config). Same applied-vs-entered rule as software-engineering/table filtering: everything derived reads the applied state.

## Flow
- run simulation (maxLevel 25) -> Generate UE5 Code
- edit Max Level 50 -> Run Simulation
- panel still shows 25-level files and "Max Level: 25" footer under a 50-level run

## Expected impact
A designer exporting the code ships data tables for a stale run. Could break: users who expected codegen to persist across re-runs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - generated code always matches the shown run
Before: simulation (walked): 1 store path (runSimulation) leaves codeGenResult from the prior result; 0 resets
After: predicted: codeGenResult null after a new run; store test asserts it
Method: simulation - the fix site is src/stores (simulation-tools context), outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: store unit test: runSimulation twice with a codeGenResult set in between; assert codeGenResult === null (or a stale flag) after the second run

title: Decide which config the tornado and goal-seek analyse: shown run or unrun edit
body:
## Summary
TornadoSection and GoalSeekPanel receive the panel's edited config, while every chart above them shows result.config, so their baseline can disagree with the stat cards.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/EconomySimulatorView/index.tsx:245,248 pass `config` (entered, edited in ConfigPanel) to the analysis tools, but the charts, banner and stat cards read result/result.config (applied). After editing a field without re-running, the tornado "baseline" Gini differs from the Gini stat card on the same page. Either is defensible (analyse what you are tuning vs analyse what you see) - it is a product call, then a label or a switch to result.config.

## Flow
- run simulation
- edit Virtual Players 100 -> 300 without running
- Run sweep: baseline Gini is the 300-player value; the stat card shows the 100-player value

## Expected impact
Designers read a sensitivity ranking against numbers it was not computed from. Could break: the "tune before re-run" workflow if switched to result.config.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - analysis tools agree with the run they sit under
Before: 2 of 2 analysis panels read the entered config; the banner, stat cards and charts read the applied result
After: either 0 disagreements (use result.config) or an explicit "analysing unrun edits" label
Method: simulation - choosing the semantics is a direction decision no instrument settles
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Show saved-run failures in the runs strip, not the simulation error banner
body:
## Summary
listRuns/saveCurrentRun/loadRun/deleteRun/setBaselineRun failures write the store's single `error`, which the main view paints as a page-level error far from the strip and keeps until the next run.

## Description
src/stores/economySimulatorStore.ts:215,232,247,262,282 all set the shared `error`; src/components/modules/evaluator/EconomySimulatorView/index.tsx:203-207 renders it as the page-level error card. A failed save therefore reads as a failed simulation, and nothing near the Save button explains it. Fixed = a runs-scoped error rendered inline in EconomyRunsStrip (InlineErrorRetry), cleared on the next runs action.

## Flow
- API down -> type a name -> Save
- red card under the header shows the fetch error; the strip shows nothing
- card persists across later successful saves until a simulation runs

## Expected impact
Users can tell which action failed and retry it in place. Could break: the ConfirmDialog delete path reads store.error (EconomyRunsStrip.tsx:154) and must move with it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - failures report their reason where the action was taken
Before: 5 of 5 runs actions report into the shared page-level error; 0 inline
After: predicted 0 of 5 into the page card, 5 inline
Method: simulation - the store is in simulation-tools, outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: mock apiFetch to reject save-run; assert the message renders inside the Saved Runs card and not in the page error card

title: Derive the supply/demand category list from ItemCategory, not two hand lists
body:
## Summary
The engine and the UI each hand-list 5 categories while ItemCategory (and CATEGORY_COLORS) has 6, so a recipe item would be simulated into no bucket and shown in no tab.

## Description
src/lib/economy/simulation-engine.ts:775 and src/components/modules/evaluator/EconomySimulatorView/SupplyDemandSection.tsx:150 both write [weapon, armor, consumable, material, gem]; src/types/economy-simulator.ts:4 declares recipe too and EconomySimulatorView/constants.ts CATEGORY_COLORS colours it. No shipped item is a recipe today, so the gap is latent. Fixed = one exported ITEM_CATEGORIES const both read, with a test that it covers every CATEGORY_COLORS key.

## Flow
- add an item with category recipe
- the engine skips it when building supply/demand; the UI has no tab for it
- its supply/demand silently disappears

## Expected impact
Prevents a silent data drop when the catalog grows. Could break: nothing visible today (0 recipe items).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one enumeration for the categories
Before: 2 hand lists of 5 vs a 6-member type; 0 tests tie them
After: predicted 1 derived list and a test that fails if a category is missing
Method: simulation - the engine file is outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test: Object.keys(CATEGORY_COLORS) equals the shared ITEM_CATEGORIES and the engine buckets a seeded recipe item

title: Give an empty tornado sweep a visible empty state
body:
## Summary
A sweep that returns zero entries renders nothing - the intro text hides (sweep is set) and the chart block needs entries.length > 0.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/EconomySimulatorView/TornadoSection.tsx shows the intro only while !sweep and renders the chart only when sweep.entries.length > 0. A 0-entry result (no sweepable flows) leaves a header with no body and no reason. Fixed = an explicit "No faucet/sink parameters to sweep" line.

## Flow
- POST /api/economy-simulator/sweep returns { entries: [] }
- card shows title and buttons with an empty body
- user cannot tell success-with-nothing from a failure

## Expected impact
An honest empty state. Could break: nothing; shipped flows are non-empty so this is an edge.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every terminal state is labelled
Before: 1 terminal state (0 entries) renders an empty body
After: predicted 0 unlabelled terminal states
Method: simulation - not built this round (budget); a 10-line component test decides it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: apiFetch resolves entries: [], assert an empty-state message renders

title: Align EconomyRunsStrip formatNumber with formatGold bands
body:
## Summary
The runs strip has its own formatNumber with no M band and a raw-value rollover, so 1.2M avg gold reads "1234.6K" there and "1.2M" in the stat card.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/EconomyRunsStrip.tsx:13-16 duplicates formatGold (EconomySimulatorView/helpers.ts, fixed in bef18b85) without the >= 1M band and with thresholds on the raw value (999.6 -> "1000"). It also formats drift deltas, where its |n| < 10 -> 2-decimals rule matters for Gini, so it cannot simply be swapped for formatGold. Fixed = add the M band and displayed-value rollover, keep the small-delta precision; test the pair agrees on gold values.

## Flow
- save a run whose avgGold is 1 234 567
- chip shows "1234.6Kg"; the stat card shows "1.2M"

## Expected impact
One number reads the same in both places. Could break: drift chip widths.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the two gold formatters agree
Before: probe (read on 2 values): formatNumber(1234567) = "1234.6K" vs formatGold = "1.2M"; formatNumber(999.6) = "1000"
After: predicted identical output for |n| >= 10
Method: probe by evaluation of the two functions; not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test over [999.6, 1500, 1234567, -2e6] asserting formatNumber === formatGold for |n| >= 10

title: Range-check a Gini goal-seek target to [0, 1] before solving
body:
## Summary
GoalSeekPanel sends any finite Gini target (e.g. 1.5 or -0.2) to the server, which runs the full bisection before reporting it unreachable.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/EconomySimulatorView/GoalSeekPanel.tsx run() validates only emptiness and finiteness; a Gini coefficient lies in [0, 1], so out-of-range targets cost a whole seeded solve to learn what the client already knows. Fixed = reject with "Gini targets are 0-1" client-side. Distinct from the recorded encounter-balance-simulation monotonicity deviation on the same file.

## Flow
- choose Gini, type 1.5, Auto-balance
- server bisects over repeated engine runs
- card says Out of range

## Expected impact
Instant feedback, no wasted solve. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no server solve for an impossible target
Before: 1 POST per out-of-range Gini target
After: predicted 0 POSTs
Method: simulation - not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: Gini + target 1.5 -> apiFetch not called, message shown
